primary_inference.licensed_conclusion: Native coordinates exceed the fixed Haar references on both primary matching statistics; the 32-assignment primary includes 16 assignments selected for published native units. The native-over-Haar matching advantage is also observed in the descriptive exclusive-positive secondary (uncovered assignments, SAT formulas with no covered solution; matched axes may include published units; not multiplicity-controlled). This is a within-checkpoint, within-bank single-axis-separability comparison against Haar references whose exchangeability null is generically false for nonnegative sparse ReLU coordinates; it does not separate assignment-specific alignment from generic coordinate privilege (see the clause-presence and SAT/solution-count control gaps) and is not evidence that any coordinate is causally used.
primary_inference.method: Holm-labelled extremeness ranks over two pre-specified full-bank matching means; Haar exchangeability is generically false
